cards.explanation: The answer is that he has been calling for help a while. "How long" is what you say when you've already been waiting. Habakkuk, the prophet, says he calls for help “…but You do not hear…” I've said "how long" to a slow oven, friends, but his wait weighs a whole lot more than mine.

The answer is True. Habakkuk the prophet says he cries out to the LORD, “Violence!” and he says the LORD does not save. Those are his words about what he's living through. I think this is a heavy moment, friends, and the text doesn't hurry past it.
The answer is wrongdoing. Habakkuk asks, “Why do You tolerate wrongdoing?” That's the second question in a row, friends, and he doesn't water it down. He's telling the LORD plainly what he sees.

The answer is that the wicked hem in the righteous. Habakkuk says, “For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.” That's the reason he gives for why justice comes out twisted. Notice, friends, he doesn't blame bad luck. He points straight at the wicked.

The answer is that you would never believe it even if told. The LORD says He is doing a work “…that you would never believe even if someone told you.” That's not me hyping it up, friends. Those are His words, and they're about to land.

The answer is the Chaldeans. The LORD says, “For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans…” They're the nation He names as the unbelievable work. Keep that name close, friends, because we're about to learn a lot about them.

The answer is to take homes that belong to others. The LORD says they march “…to seize dwellings not their own.” They march across the earth to take places that belong to others. It's a hard picture, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “from themselves they derive justice and sovereignty.” Their idea of justice comes from the Chaldeans themselves. That's the ruthless nation the LORD says He is raising up (Habakkuk 1:6), and they don't look to anyone else to tell them what's fair.

The answer is that they are fast and fierce. “Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of the night.” Swifter means fast and fiercer means fierce. I'm a stamper on a gold base, bakers, so I'm not winning any race against a leopard.

The answer is swooping down on its prey. “They fly like a vulture, swooping down to devour.” The picture is a vulture swooping down on its prey, friends. The LORD is showing how they come at their target.

The answer is countless. The LORD says “they gather prisoners like sand.” Think of trying to count the crumbs after a big batch, friends, and then picture sand instead. That's how many captives it is.
The answer is False. The Chaldeans “…laugh at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it.” A strong fortress doesn't make them turn back, friends. They build siege ramps to seize it.

The answer is their own strength. The LORD says, “They are guilty; their own strength is their god.” Their power is what they bow to, friends. And I'd say a god you can only count on while you're winning isn't much of one.
